legs.target: CTO condition: print the transcripts key ARN beside the request_compositions key ARN
legs.proof_required: they must DIFFER; equal is a STOP
legs.proof: THE TWO KEYS DIFFER, MEASURED LIVE AT BOTH GRAINS OF THE request_compositions STORE. TRANSCRIPTS KEY (the key aws_kms_grant.commentary at commentary.tf:267 grants Decrypt/GenerateDataKey/DescribeKey on): arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:313476888478:key/44a2284f-1e14-4ea1-b6cb-f6121bfde35a, read live by `kms describe-key --key-id alias/opal-data-transcripts` (the alias aws_kms_alias.transcripts mints at main.tf:173, alias/${local.bucket}), description "Encrypts every object in the Opal meeting-transcripts bucket. Use is granted to named readers only." REQUEST_COMPOSITIONS STORE KEY: arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:313476888478:key/7f4d3042-10d8-49a7-b55e-3c963cea8111. The condition names one key but the store has TWO grains and the half's purpose (its lines 20-21: the grant does not reopen msg 2341 only if the transcripts key does not encrypt request_compositions) is only answered by reading both, so both were read: (i) DynamoDB -- `describe-table --table-name irpt-requests` (the table every request_compositions policy addresses as data.terraform_remote_state.core.outputs.tables.requests) reads SSEType KMS, Status ENABLED, KMSMasterKeyArn 7f4d3042-10d8-49a7-b55e-3c963cea8111; (ii) S3 -- the irpt PRODUCT bucket, resolved FROM THE LGIC REGISTRY and never typed (infra/logic/registry/scopes.json, key irpt, class PRODUCT -> opal-data-irpt, the same derivation ops/iam.tf:134 uses so the grant and the address cannot name different buckets), reads a default of SSEAlgorithm aws:kms with KMSMasterKeyID 7f4d3042-10d8-49a7-b55e-3c963cea8111, which is where the state/request_compositions family lands. BOTH GRAINS RESOLVE TO THE SAME KEY AND NEITHER IS THE TRANSCRIPTS KEY: 44a2284f != 7f4d3042. So the transcripts key does not encrypt request_compositions, the commentary grant is confined to the transcripts stack's own key for its queues and logs, and msg 2341's prohibition on kms:Decrypt over IRPT's request_compositions is not reopened by it. No STOP. Note on the instrument: this is an EXISTENCE-AND-EQUALITY read of two live key ARNs, not an IAM simulation -- the simulator's verdicts are leg SIM's, and a key-policy-only grant reads implicitDeny there, so the key policy is read where the simulator is blind as the order requires.
